title: PSVR2 not recognized by PS5
shortDescription: PS5 console does not detect the connected headset.
fullDescription: PSVR2 connects via a single USB-C cable to the PS5 front port. The port must provide full USB-C power and data. Dust, loose seating, or PS5 firmware can prevent detection.
symptoms: No VR icon on PS5 menu

fixSteps.title: Reseat USB-C
fixSteps.instruction: Fully insert cable into PS5 front USB-C.

whenToCallPro: If a replacement headset cable does not resolve, contact PlayStation Support.

faq.a: Yes, via Sony's official PC adapter.

title: Headset tracking drifts or freezes
shortDescription: Inside-out cameras fail to establish tracking.
fullDescription: PSVR2 uses four cameras for inside-out tracking. Poor lighting, reflective floors, or dirty lenses disrupt tracking.

fixSteps.title: Clean cameras
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the four camera lenses with microfiber.

whenToCallPro: If tracking fails after factory reset.

title: Sense controller not paired or offline
shortDescription: PS5 cannot see one or both Sense controllers.
fullDescription: Sense controllers pair via Bluetooth to the PS5, not the headset. If pairing is lost, re-pair via USB-C.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair via USB
fixSteps.instruction: Connect each controller to PS5 with USB-C for 30 seconds.

title: See-through view fails
shortDescription: Passthrough cameras show black or distorted image.
fullDescription: Passthrough uses the same tracking cameras. A firmware bug or dirty lens can break the view.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Check PS5 settings for PSVR2 firmware update.

title: HDR appears washed out or too dark
shortDescription: OLED HDR on PSVR2 not calibrated correctly.
fullDescription: PSVR2 has HDR OLED panels. Incorrect PS5 HDR calibration or system-level HDR mismatch causes washed image.

fixSteps.title: Recalibrate HDR
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Screen and Video > PSVR2 > Adjust HDR.

faq.a: Yes, but you'll lose OLED punch.

title: Visible graininess on OLED panels
fullDescription: Mura is a characteristic of OLED where individual pixels vary slightly in brightness, visible as grain in dark scenes.

fixSteps.title: Raise black level
fixSteps.instruction: Adjust HDR to reduce visible grain.

fixSteps.title: RMA for severe mura
fixSteps.instruction: Contact Sony if mura is extreme.

whenToCallPro: For severe mura contact PlayStation Support.

faq.a: Mild mura is expected in OLED.

title: Motion sickness on fast movement
fullDescription: Motion sickness is reduced by correct IPD, high framerate, and comfort options in games.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate IPD
fixSteps.instruction: Adjust lens distance using knob on headset.

fixSteps.title: Enable comfort settings
fixSteps.instruction: Turn on vignette and teleport locomotion.

faq.a: Yes, correct IPD reduces strain and nausea.

title: Buzz in PSVR2 headphones
shortDescription: Grounding or interference noise in earbuds.
fullDescription: Some users hear static via the built-in 3.5mm jack, traced to grounding or EMI.

title: PSVR2 firmware update fails
fullDescription: Update failures are typically from unplugging the headset mid-flash or PS5 storage issues.

fixSteps.title: Retry without touching cable
fixSteps.instruction: Re-run update and leave PSVR2 stationary.

whenToCallPro: If headset remains bricked, RMA via Sony.

title: Eye tracking cannot calibrate
shortDescription: User's eyes not detected by internal cameras.
fullDescription: Eye tracking requires clean lenses and proper IPD. Contacts or glasses can impact calibration.

fixSteps.title: Clean inner lenses
fixSteps.instruction: Use microfiber to wipe the inside lenses gently.

fixSteps.title: Adjust IPD
fixSteps.instruction: Use headset IPD dial during calibration.

faq.q: Does eye tracking work with glasses?
